nodes.prompt: What does it take to rise in the Guild?

AGHallGuildMaster: Staying alive, mostly. Do honest work, often, and when your reputation and experience are enough, the Guild will recognize your growth.
The higher your rank, the harder the jobs available, but the better the rewards.
We rank all adventurers from E through A, though those truly exceptional can achieve an S rank.

nodes.prompt: Did you ever make S-rank yourself?

AGHallGuildMaster: No. That takes deeds people sing about, and only one in a lifetime is ever worthy. I'm just a proud old man at the back of the room now.

nodes.prompt: How should I spend what I earn?

AGHallGuildMaster: On yourself. Appraisal first, so you know what you're looking at. Then the drills, so you live through it. Books and Augments after that.

nodes.prompt: And those Guild Boxes?

AGHallGuildMaster: A bit risky if you ask me, but a good way to get your hands on some fine gear. It'll cost you some of your reputation as well as merit and gold.
I always preferred to earn my gear the old-fashioned way.

nodes.prompt: Should I travel alone?

AGHallGuildMaster: No. Alone is how we lose good adventurers. Find people you trust and register as a party.
The longer you share the road, the more you hold each other up.
My advice is to make sure you travel with those who complement your strengths and cover your weaknesses.
The Frostbitten lived by that, and it's no wonder they reached the top of the board.

nodes.prompt: Where does the Guild stand on the war?

AGHallGuildMaster: Nowhere, and we've sworn to it. No war contracts, no taking sides. You see how empty this place is? Damn wars are the reason, Oblivion take them all.

nodes.prompt: And the Thalmor?

AGHallGuildMaster: We've no quarrel with them. That's what I say out loud. Keep your voice down when you ask that.

nodes.prompt: Does the Guild care what its members get up to?

AGHallGuildMaster: The Guild? Only when a Jarl does. Me? I'd like to think we're the ones who come when the farmer's scared. Try to stay on that side of things.
And if not? Well, try not to get caught.

nodes.prompt: Tell me about what you do here.

AGHallAssistant: I'm the one who reads the reports adventurers bring back and who directs the Guild's scouts. Which interests you?

nodes.prompt: What do the scouts know?

AGHallAssistant: Where each hold's dungeons are, and how badly each is likely to treat you. Any counter can mark your map for some merit.

nodes.prompt: I could just go and look.

AGHallAssistant: You could. Many have. I have their reports, from those who wrote any.

nodes.prompt: Who reads all those reports?

AGHallAssistant: I read every one. Then they go on the shelves, where they may save anyone who bothers to read first.

nodes.prompt: What about a dungeon I clear with no contract?

AGHallAssistant: Report it all the same. The Guild pays for any dungeon cleared, contract or no, at any counter. Each is paid once, so spare me the second account.

nodes.prompt: Could you tell me about the guild counter?

AGHallClerkDay: Work goes out, reports come back, you sell me your trophies, and there's plenty to buy.
The innkeepers run counters of their own, but this one's the biggest.

AGHallClerkEvening: Nearly everything the Guild does goes through here! Taking work, selling trophies, buying what you need.
The innkeepers keep counters too, in every hold capital.

Notices are requests that could come from anywhere in Skyrim.
There's always bounties posted by the jarls of each hold as well if that's more your thing.
Get out there and visit the boards in each town to find new postings; we'll try to keep the board in the hall up to date with what you come across.

nodes.prompt: How do I get paid?

AGHallClerkDay: Finish the job and bring your report to any counter to earn Guild merit and reputation.
Note that the Guild also pays gold for reports of a cleared dungeon.

AGHallClerkEvening: Just hand your report in at any counter when the job's done! That earns you merit and reputation.
Cleared dungeons are worth reporting too, plus those pay gold.

nodes.prompt: You said I can sell trophies?

AGHallClerkDay: Hides, claws, teeth, anything off a proper monster. Hand them in at any guild counter and we'll pay you in merit based on their fair market value.

AGHallClerkEvening: Yes! Bring them to any counter and we'll pay merit for anything you've taken from a monster, depending on what it's worth.
Don't tell me how you pulled the parts out though. I'd rather not know.

nodes.prompt: What sort of things can I buy here?

AGHallClerkDay: Plenty! We offer training, a unique Appraisal skill, useful books, spell tomes, potions, and more.
Augments are a day's edge: carry more, haggle better, learn faster. Guild Boxes are a chance for a powerful item once your rank is high enough.

AGHallClerkEvening: We have training, spell tomes, potions and books, and Appraisal teaches you to size up threats and evaluate the true value of items.
An Augment gives you a boon for about a day. Once your rank is high enough, a Guild Box might hold something wonderful... if you can afford it!

nodes.prompt: What do I do with my guild card?

AGHallClerkDay: Show it, mostly. It says the Guild vouches for you.
Keep it safe: a replacement costs coin, and you'll have to ask each hold to replace any stamps from your lost card.

AGHallClerkEvening: It shows your rank and how far you've come. So please don't lose it!
Any counter can make you a new one for a small fee, but you'd need each hold to stamp it again.

nodes.prompt: What are the stamps for?

AGHallClerkDay: Proof of where you've done real work. Report enough dungeons from a hold, and the counter in its capital will stamp your card with their crest.
Merchants there might give you better prices for making them safer.

AGHallClerkEvening: They show which holds you've helped! Clear and report enough dungeons, then visit the inn in its capital to get your card stamped.
I've heard the merchants there might thank you with a better price.

nodes.prompt: How do I form a party?

AGHallClerkDay: Bring your group to the counter, pay a small fee, and give me a name you'd want shouted in a tavern. Anyone not on our ledger, I can sign on as well.

AGHallClerkEvening: You'll need at least one companion with you! If they aren't Guild members yet, I can sign them up.
Then there's a small fee, and you get to choose a name! That's the best part.

nodes.prompt: You mentioned the innkeepers?

AGHallClerkDay: Every hold capital's inn keeps a counter for us. Reports, trophies, supplies and that hold's work, all without the walk back here.
Some things like promotions, training, and the good inventory are only available here in the guild hall.

AGHallClerkEvening: You can hand in reports, sell trophies and find that hold's work at any of their counters, so you won't have to walk all the way back here.
Promotions, training and the best goods stay at the hall, though, so I'll still get to see you!
